title: Undistort
summary: Remove lens distortion and write a dataset in the layout trainers expect

blocks.text:
Notebook 03 found barrel distortion in the kit lens at 18 mm: straight lines near the edges bow outwards. gsplat renders with an ideal pinhole camera, where straight lines stay straight. Training on the distorted frames would leave every image slightly out of agreement with the renders near its edges.

So here I resample every frame as if it had been taken by a perfect pinhole camera, and convert the reconstruction to match. The output is `work/dataset/`, in the layout Gaussian Splatting trainers expect:

```
work/dataset/
├── images/          undistorted images
└── sparse/0/        cameras.bin (PINHOLE), images.bin, points3D.bin, …
```

import shutil, tempfile, time
from pathlib import Path

import cv2
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import pycolmap

pycolmap.logging.minloglevel = 2

PROJECT_DIR = Path.cwd()
WORK_DIR = PROJECT_DIR / "work"
IMAGES_DIR = WORK_DIR / "images"            # input: distorted images (notebook 01)
MODEL_DIR = WORK_DIR / "sparse" / "0"       # input: GLOMAP reconstruction (notebook 03)
DATASET_DIR = WORK_DIR / "dataset"          # output

rec = pycolmap.Reconstruction(MODEL_DIR)
cam = rec.cameras[next(iter(rec.cameras))]
print(f"input model: {rec.num_reg_images()} images, {rec.num_points3D():,} points")
print("input camera:", cam)

## What undistortion does

The `OPENCV` camera model has two parts: a pinhole projection (`u = fx · X/Z + cx`, `v = fy · Y/Z + cy`), and distortion terms (`k1, k2, p1, p2`) that move each pixel a little, more so towards the edges. Undistorting means defining a new `PINHOLE` camera with only `fx, fy, cx, cy`, and then, for every pixel of the new image: turn it into a viewing direction, find where the real lens saw that direction, and copy the colour from there with bilinear interpolation.

How far each pixel moves:

h, w = cam.height, cam.width
ys, xs = np.mgrid[0:h:8, 0:w:8].astype(float)
pinhole_px = np.stack([xs.ravel(), ys.ravel()], axis=1)

# 1) pixel of an ideal pinhole camera with the same fx, fy, cx, cy -> viewing direction
rays = np.stack([(pinhole_px[:, 0] - cam.principal_point_x) / cam.focal_length_x,
                 (pinhole_px[:, 1] - cam.principal_point_y) / cam.focal_length_y,
                 np.ones(len(pinhole_px))], axis=1)
# 2) where the real, distorted camera sees that direction
distorted_px = cam.img_from_cam(rays)
shift = np.linalg.norm(distorted_px - pinhole_px, axis=1).reshape(xs.shape)

plt.figure(figsize=(10, 5.5))
plt.imshow(shift, extent=(0, w, h, 0), cmap="magma")
plt.colorbar(label="pixel shift caused by the lens")
plt.contour(xs, ys, shift, levels=[1, 5, 10, 20, 40], colors="white", linewidths=0.7)
plt.title(f"Distortion: centre ≈ 0 px, corners ≈ {shift.max():.0f} px")
plt.show()

Near the centre the lens is almost perfect; towards the corners pixels move by tens of pixels. That's a lot compared with the sub-pixel reprojection error from notebook 03.

## Cropping

With barrel distortion the undistorted image gets pulled outwards at the edges, and parts of the new rectangle have no source pixels. COLMAP's `blank_pixels` decides what happens there: `0` (the default) crops until no black pixels remain, losing a thin strip of the original; `1` keeps all original pixels and leaves black corners.

I crop. Black corners would look like real image content to the trainer, which would try to reproduce them with dark floaters. Both options on one frame:

# Demo image: the one with the most matched features in its top-left corner, where distortion is
# strongest. That's usually a view where the corner shows table texture rather than smooth pumpkin skin.
def corner_features(im):
    return sum(1 for p in im.points2D if p.has_point3D() and p.xy[0] < 0.3 * cam.width and p.xy[1] < 0.35 * cam.height)
demo_name = max(rec.images.values(), key=corner_features).name
print("demo image:", demo_name)

def undistort_one(name, blank_pixels):
    options = pycolmap.UndistortCameraOptions()
    options.blank_pixels = blank_pixels
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
        pycolmap.undistort_images(tmp, MODEL_DIR, IMAGES_DIR, image_names=[name], undistort_options=options)
        img = cv2.cvtColor(cv2.imread(str(Path(tmp) / "images" / name)), cv2.COLOR_BGR2RGB)
        new_cam = pycolmap.Reconstruction(Path(tmp) / "sparse").cameras[1]
    return img, new_cam

original = cv2.cvtColor(cv2.imread(str(IMAGES_DIR / demo_name)), cv2.COLOR_BGR2RGB)
cropped, cam_cropped = undistort_one(demo_name, 0.0)
full, cam_full = undistort_one(demo_name, 1.0)

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(18, 4.2))
for ax, img, title in zip(axes, [original, full, cropped],
                          [f"original (distorted) {original.shape[1]}×{original.shape[0]}",
                           f"undistorted, blank_pixels=1: {full.shape[1]}×{full.shape[0]}",
                           f"undistorted, blank_pixels=0 (used): {cropped.shape[1]}×{cropped.shape[0]}"]):
    ax.imshow(img); ax.set_title(title); ax.axis("off")
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
demo image: frame_00338.jpg

The middle image has black corners. The right one is cropped just enough to avoid them, and is still slightly larger than the original in pixels, because undistortion stretches the edges.

The top-left corner up close, where the distortion is strongest. Edges between the wood blocks that bend in the original should be straighter after:

def corner(img, size=420):
    return img[:size, :int(size * 16 / 9)]

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(16, 5))
axes[0].imshow(corner(original)); axes[0].set_title("original: top-left corner")
axes[1].imshow(corner(cropped)); axes[1].set_title("undistorted: top-left corner")
for ax in axes:
    ax.axis("off")
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()

## Undistorting all frames

`undistort_images` writes the undistorted images to `dataset/images/` and a converted reconstruction to `dataset/sparse/`, with the new `PINHOLE` camera and every 2D keypoint moved to its undistorted position, so the 3D points still line up. It also prepares input for dense reconstruction (`stereo/` and `run-colmap-*.sh`), which I don't need here.

if DATASET_DIR.exists():
    shutil.rmtree(DATASET_DIR)

undistort_options = pycolmap.UndistortCameraOptions()
undistort_options.blank_pixels = 0.0                     # crop: no black borders

t0 = time.time()
pycolmap.undistort_images(
    output_path=DATASET_DIR,
    input_path=MODEL_DIR,
    image_path=IMAGES_DIR,
    output_type="COLMAP",
    undistort_options=undistort_options,
)
print(f"undistorted in {time.time() - t0:.0f} s")
print("written:", sorted(p.name for p in DATASET_DIR.iterdir()))

undistorted in 10 s
written: ['images', 'run-colmap-geometric.sh', 'run-colmap-photometric.sh', 'sparse', 'stereo']

### Standard layout

Gaussian Splatting tools (gsplat, the original 3DGS code, Brush, LichtFeld Studio and others) expect `images/` plus the model in `sparse/0/`. So I move the model there and delete the dense-reconstruction files.

sparse_tmp = DATASET_DIR / "sparse_tmp"
(DATASET_DIR / "sparse").rename(sparse_tmp)
(DATASET_DIR / "sparse").mkdir()
sparse_tmp.rename(DATASET_DIR / "sparse" / "0")

shutil.rmtree(DATASET_DIR / "stereo", ignore_errors=True)
for script in DATASET_DIR.glob("run-colmap-*.sh"):
    script.unlink()

DATASET_MODEL_DIR = DATASET_DIR / "sparse" / "0"
for p in sorted(DATASET_DIR.rglob("*")):
    if p.is_dir():
        n_files = sum(1 for _ in p.iterdir())
        print(f"{str(p.relative_to(DATASET_DIR)) + '/':<14} {n_files} files")

images/        194 files
sparse/        1 files
sparse/0/      5 files

## Checking the result

### The new camera

und = pycolmap.Reconstruction(DATASET_MODEL_DIR)
new_cam = und.cameras[next(iter(und.cameras))]
print("before:", cam)
print("after :", new_cam)
print(f"\n{und.num_reg_images()} images, {und.num_points3D():,} points (unchanged: "
      f"{und.num_reg_images() == rec.num_reg_images() and und.num_points3D() == rec.num_points3D()})")

The camera is now `PINHOLE` with the same focal length: undistortion straightens, it doesn't zoom. The image grew, and the principal point moved to its new centre. Poses and 3D points are unchanged.

The same data in COLMAP's text format (the trainer reads the binary version):

with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
    und.write_text(tmp)
    for fname, n_lines in [("cameras.txt", 4), ("images.txt", 6), ("points3D.txt", 5)]:
        lines = (Path(tmp) / fname).read_text().splitlines()
        print(f"── {fname} ──")
        for line in lines[:n_lines]:
            print("  " + (line[:150] + " …" if len(line) > 150 else line))
        print()

- `cameras.txt`: `CAMERA_ID MODEL WIDTH HEIGHT fx fy cx cy`.
- `images.txt`: two lines per image. The first is the world-to-camera pose, as a quaternion `QW QX QY QZ` and a translation `TX TY TZ`. The second lists the 2D keypoints with the 3D point each one observes (`-1` = none).
- `points3D.txt`: `ID X Y Z R G B ERROR`, then the track: which images, and which keypoint in each, see the point.

### Do the 3D points still line up?

If the conversion is consistent, the reprojection error with the pinhole camera should be about the same as before. I recompute it from scratch instead of trusting the stored values:

rec.update_point_3d_errors()
und.update_point_3d_errors()
err_before = rec.compute_mean_reprojection_error()
err_after = und.compute_mean_reprojection_error()
print(f"mean reprojection error, distorted model  : {err_before:.3f} px")
print(f"mean reprojection error, undistorted model: {err_after:.3f} px")

mean reprojection error, distorted model  : 0.911 px
mean reprojection error, undistorted model: 0.946 px

It went up by a few hundredths of a pixel. Undistortion stretches the image towards the edges, so an error of 1 px near a corner of the original becomes a bit more than 1 px afterwards.

The 3D points projected into an undistorted frame, including the corner where the distortion was strongest:

im = und.find_image_with_name(demo_name)
img = cv2.cvtColor(cv2.imread(str(DATASET_DIR / "images" / demo_name)), cv2.COLOR_BGR2RGB)
xyz = np.array([und.points3D[p.point3D_id].xyz for p in im.points2D if p.has_point3D()])
uv = new_cam.img_from_cam(im.cam_from_world() * xyz)                 # pinhole projection
rgb = np.array([und.points3D[p.point3D_id].color for p in im.points2D if p.has_point3D()]) / 255

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(18, 5.5))
axes[0].imshow(img); axes[0].scatter(*uv.T, s=6, c="lime")
axes[0].set_title(f"{demo_name}: {len(uv)} 3D points projected with the PINHOLE camera")
axes[1].imshow(corner(img)); in_corner = (uv[:, 0] < 420 * 16 / 9) & (uv[:, 1] < 420)
axes[1].scatter(*uv[in_corner].T, s=25, facecolors="none", edgecolors="lime")
axes[1].set_title("zoom: top-left corner")
for ax in axes:
    ax.axis("off")
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()

The points sit on the texture details they were triangulated from.

## Checks

n_images = len(list((DATASET_DIR / "images").iterdir()))
files_ok = all((DATASET_MODEL_DIR / f).exists() for f in ("cameras.bin", "images.bin", "points3D.bin"))
checks = {
    f"{n_images} undistorted images written": n_images == und.num_reg_images(),
    "model in dataset/sparse/0 (cameras/images/points3D.bin)": files_ok,
    f"camera is PINHOLE ({new_cam.model_name})": new_cam.model_name == "PINHOLE",
    f"reprojection error about the same ({err_before:.3f} → {err_after:.3f} px)": abs(err_after - err_before) < 0.1,
}
for name, ok in checks.items():
    print(f"{'ok  ' if ok else 'FAIL'} {name}")
total_mb = sum(p.stat().st_size for p in DATASET_DIR.rglob("*") if p.is_file()) / 1024**2
print(f"\ndataset size: {total_mb:.0f} MB")

ok   194 undistorted images written
ok   model in dataset/sparse/0 (cameras/images/points3D.bin)
ok   camera is PINHOLE (PINHOLE)
ok   reprojection error about the same (0.911 → 0.946 px)

dataset size: 226 MB

## Result

`work/dataset/` holds 194 undistorted frames and the converted model in `sparse/0/`: a `PINHOLE` camera with the same poses and points. The reprojection error rose by a few hundredths of a pixel. The layout also works with other 3DGS tools, not just gsplat.
